items.title: The one-dimensional continuity identity and the constant flux of stationary solutions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be nonempty open intervals
([[def-interval]]), and let $V:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be a function. Let
$u,v:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ be functions whose partial derivatives
$\partial_tu,\partial_tv,\partial_xu,\partial_xv,\partial_x^2u,\partial_x^2v$
exist and are continuous on $\Omega\times I$
([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-derivative]]) and satisfy the pair of
equations
$$\hbar\,\partial_tu=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2v+Vv,\qquad -\hbar\,\partial_tv=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2u+Vu$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$. Write $\psi:=u+iv$ for the corresponding
$\mathbb C$-valued function with component functions $u$ and $v$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]), so that the two
displayed equations are the componentwise reading of
$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2\psi+V\psi$. Put
$$n(x,t):=|\psi(x,t)|^2=u(x,t)^2+v(x,t)^2,\qquad j(x,t):=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\!\bigl(\overline{\psi(x,t)}\,\partial_x\psi(x,t)\bigr) =\frac{\hbar}{m}\bigl(u\,\partial_xv-(\partial_xu)\,v\bigr)(x,t).$$
Then:

(a) *Continuity identity.* $\partial_tn(x,t)+\partial_xj(x,t)=0$ for every
$(x,t)\in\Omega\times I$.

(b) *Constant flux of stationary solutions.* If in addition $u,v:\Omega\to
\mathbb R$ have continuous second derivatives and there are a real $E$ and a
real-valued $V$ with
$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}u''+Vu=Eu$ and $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}v''+Vv=Ev$ pointwise on
$\Omega$, then the function $x\mapsto j(x):=\frac{\hbar}{m}(uv'-u'v)(x)$ is
constant on $\Omega$.

The assertion is an identity for the declared differentiable functions and
the declared real pair $V$; it constructs no probability law, no state and no
physical interpretation.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 2.3, printed pages 32-33 (PDF pages 40-41): the probability current and the continuity equation in the position representation

items.title: The one-dimensional free Schr"odinger operator as the weak second-derivative operator
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=2\pi^2\hbar^2/m$, and let $H_0$ be the free one-dimensional operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=1$, this $c$ and $b=0$:
$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^{*}M_{c|\xi|^2}\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C):|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal F_2$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem and
$M_{c|\xi|^2}$ is multiplication by the function $\xi\mapsto c|\xi|^2$. Let
$D^2$ denote the second weak derivative, defined componentwise on the
locally integrable classes of $\mathbb R$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), and let
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ as sets and
$$H_0f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\,D^2f\qquad\text{for every }f\in D(H_0);$$
equivalently, $\mathcal F_2(H_0f)(\xi)=c|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f(\xi)$ and
$\mathcal F_2\bigl(-\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2f\bigr)(\xi)=c|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$, and the two $L^2$ classes agree.

(b) For every real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the operator
$H_0+M_V$ of clause (c) of the cited theorem, with domain $D(H_0)$, coincides
with the operator $f\mapsto-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2f+Vf$ on the same domain; in
particular, for $E\in\mathbb R$ and $\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ the
eigenvalue equation $(H_0+M_V)\psi=E\psi$ is equivalent to the weak equation
$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ elementwise in $L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$.

The statement identifies operators on the same domain; it asserts neither
smoothness of the classes in $W^{2,2}$ nor any physical interpretation.

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 2.1, printed pages 20-27 (PDF pages 23-30): the one-dimensional free Schroedinger equation and its kinetic operator

items.title: Positive scalar multiples of self-adjoint operators: domains, resolvents, spectra and eigenbases
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a
densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $c>0$ be
real. Write $cA$ for the operator with domain $D(cA):=D(A)$ and
$(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$. Then:

(a) $cA$ is self-adjoint.

(b) For every $z\in\mathbb C$ one has $z\in\rho(cA)$ if and only if
$z/c\in\rho(A)$, and then
$(cA-z)^{-1}=c^{-1}(A-z/c)^{-1}$; consequently
$\rho(cA)=c\,\rho(A)$ and $\sigma(cA)=c\,\sigma(A)$.

(c) If some, hence every, resolvent of $A$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]), then every resolvent of $cA$ is compact and
$A$ and $cA$ have the same complete orthonormal eigenfamily $(e_j)_{j\in J}$.
If $N:=\dim H<\infty$, take $J=\{1,\ldots,N\}$; if $H$ is infinite dimensional,
take $J=\mathbb N$, with $|\mu_j|\to\infty$ and each eigenvalue repeated
according to its finite multiplicity. In both cases $Ae_j=\mu_je_j$,
$(cA)e_j=c\mu_je_j$, and
$$\sigma(A)=\{\mu_j:j\in J\},\qquad\sigma(cA)=\{c\mu_j:j\in J\}$$
with no other spectral points. The finite-dimensional conclusion also holds
without a separate compactness assumption, since bounded operators on such
$H$ are compact.

(d) Eigenvectors correspond exactly: for $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in H$,
$x\ne0$, one has $x\in D(A)$ and $Ax=\lambda x$ if and only if
$x\in D(cA)$ and $(cA)x=(c\lambda)x$; and every eigenvalue of $cA$ has the same
eigenspace as the corresponding eigenvalue of $A$.

(e) If $A\ge\gamma$ in the quadratic-form sense, meaning that
$\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge\gamma\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in D(A)$, then
$cA\ge c\gamma$ in the same sense.

Only the scaling of the given operator is asserted; no domain, spectrum or
eigenvector is claimed for any other rescaling, and no physical
interpretation is attached.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.2 printed pages 58-67 (PDF pages 70-79): self-adjoint operators, adjoints and the spectrum under scaling
M. Reed and B. Simon, Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I: Functional Analysis, revised edition, Section VIII.1 (closed, symmetric and self-adjoint operators; scaling and resolvents)

items.title: The declared one-dimensional line model: state space, Hamiltonian, bound states and generalized stationary solutions
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position is
read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared effective one-dimensional model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, adopt the **line model**. Its declared state space is
$$H_{\mathrm{lin}}:=L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C\ \text{measurable}: \int_{\mathbb R}|f(x)|^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the complex Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes with the pairing
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}f\overline g\,dx$ linear in the first
argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Its declared
**position assignment** is the multiplication assignment $Q$, defined on the
classes with $xf\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}$, with the declared outcome law
$$\mu^{Q}_{\psi}(B):=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R \text{ Borel})$$
for a unit class $\psi$, the one-dimensional reading of the framework's Born
position law of [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (a)
adopted here as part of the model; its declared **momentum assignment** is
$P:=-i\hbar D$ on the classes whose weak derivative $D\psi$ lies in
$H_{\mathrm{lin}}$ ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]).
The pair asserts no derivation of $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$, $Q$ or $P$ from the
three-dimensional model $H_{0}$ of P5: the reduction to one spatial dimension,
for instance by an idealized strong transverse confinement or by a declared
one-dimensional sector, is an assumption of the model. An assignment of a
concrete material system to the line model is an identification in the sense
of clause (iii) of P7 and carries the corresponding uncertainty.

**(c) The assigned energy operator.** Let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be real,
bounded and measurable; write $\|V\|_{\infty}:=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|V(x)|$.
The **assigned energy operator** of the line model with potential $V$ is
$$H_{V}:=H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}+M_{V},\qquad H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad c:=\frac{2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}}{m},$$
with $M_{V}$ the multiplication operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (a), on the common domain
$D(H_{V}):=D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}})
=\{f\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}\}$,
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a)-(c)). The declared energy unit is the joule. By
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain
$D(H_{V})$ is the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,D^{2}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$D^{2}$ the second weak derivative, so the model's time-independent equation
inside any open interval on which $V$ is (say) constant is the ordinary
differential equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+V\psi=E\psi$. The model
adopts $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its assigned energy observable in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a); its
self-adjointness is established by the line-model energy theorem of this page
and is not presupposed here. A declared potential is **compactly supported** when $V$
vanishes almost everywhere outside some bounded interval.

**(d) Bound states and stationary vocabulary.** A **stationary solution** of
the model with potential $V$ and energy $E\in\mathbb R$ is a nonzero class
$\psi\in D(H_{V})$ with $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$; the pair $(\psi,E)$ is an
**eigenpair** of the model. A **bound state** of the model is a stationary
solution with energy $E<0$ whose representative is normalized, $\|\psi\|=1$;
its eigenvalue $E$ is its **binding energy**, read in joules, and in this model
the value $0$ is called the **continuum threshold**. The model reads the
energy outcome law of the pure preparation of a unit eigenstate $\psi$ with
eigenvalue $E$ through clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] as the point
mass $\delta_{E}$ at $E$, so that outcome in $\{E\}$ has probability one; and
the position density of the preparation is $|\psi|^{2}$ by clause (b). These
readings are declarations of the model under P2 and construct no sample,
detector or measured value.

**(e) Declared generalized stationary solutions.** Let
$-\infty=x_{0}<x_{1}<\dots<x_{n}=\infty$ be a finite partition of
$\mathbb R$, and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and classically
$C^{1}$ on $\mathbb R$ with a continuous derivative, and twice continuously
differentiable on each open interval $(x_{j},x_{j+1})$ restricted to which
$V$ is continuous, satisfying
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''(x)+V(x)\psi(x)=E\psi(x)$ there. Such a $\psi$ is
a **declared generalized stationary solution** of the model at energy $E$. It
is generally not an element of $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$ (a bounded oscillatory
solution has $|\psi|^{2}$ not integrable), so it is not a preparation of the
model and clause (d) does not apply to it; it is used only through the
declared flux quantities computed from it, and every such use states the
idealization. The pair's scattering reading assigns to $\psi$ the
**probability current** $j(x)=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{\psi(x)}\psi'(x)\bigr)$,
read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ by clause (d)5 of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and reads a ratio of currents at
infinity as a *transmitted or reflected fraction* of the incident current,
conditional on the declared solution and on the asymptotics displayed in each
statement; no such fraction is ascribed to a single particle and no count is
predicted.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the data of the pair: a declared
effective line model with a declared potential, energy operator, bound-state
vocabulary and generalized-solution vocabulary. They introduce no assumption
beyond P1, P2, P4, P5, P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; in particular the
line model, its state space and its position and momentum assignments are
declarations of the pair and are not consequences of the three-dimensional
model. No numerical value of $m$, $V$ or $\hbar$ and no measured quantity is
asserted.

items.physical_scope: The pair's declared effective one-dimensional model for a spinless massive particle: its state space, position and momentum assignments, its assigned energy operator for a real bounded measurable potential, its bound-state and stationary vocabulary, and its declared generalized stationary solutions used for the scattering reading. The model is an additional assumption of the pair, not a derivation from the three-dimensional massive-particle model P5, and no identification of a concrete apparatus or material system with the model is asserted; such an identification would be a tested identification with uncertainty in the sense of P7. No experiment and no empirical value appear.

items.title: The declared interval models with Dirichlet and Robin boundary conditions, and the declared zero-range (delta) model
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the framework postulates and units of clause (a)
of [[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]], and the vocabulary of
its clauses (b)-(f): the effective one-dimensional state space, the position
and momentum assignments, the assigned energy operator $H_{V}=H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}+M_{V}$
for a real bounded measurable potential, bound states, stationary solutions
and declared generalized stationary solutions. Fix $m>0$, $\hbar>0$ and the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Dirichlet interval model.** Fix $0<L<\infty$ and a real $V\in
C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, read as a potential energy in joules, and put
$\tilde V:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, a real continuous function on $[0,L]$ with the
dimension of an inverse square length under the conventions of the framework;
the factor $2m/\hbar^{2}$ has unit $\mathrm{J^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$, so the products
in clause (c) of the next item are dimensionally consistent. The **Dirichlet
interval model** declares the state space $L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$ of
almost-everywhere classes with the pairing linear in the first argument
([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) and the assigned energy
operator
$$H_{D,V}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{D,V}):=\{u\in H^{2}(0,L):u^{*}(0)=u^{*}(L)=0\},$$
where $D^{2}$ is the second weak derivative and $u^{*}$ the continuous
representative of [[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]]; in
the notation of [[thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-diagonal-domain-identification]]
this operator is $(\hbar^{2}/2m)(A_{D}+M_{\tilde V})$ with
$D(A_{D})=\{u\in H^{2}(0,L):u^{*}(0)=u^{*}(L)=0\}$, and for $V=0$ its
declared free eigenpairs are the pairs
$\bigl(\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}(\frac{n\pi}{L})^{2},\,e_{n}\bigr)$ with
$e_{n}(x)=\sqrt{2/L}\,\sin(n\pi x/L)$, $n\ge1$, read from
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-diagonal-domain-identification]] and
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-sine-on-completeness]]. The vanishing endpoint condition
is a declared idealization of an infinitely high wall at each endpoint; the
pair does not derive it from the line model, and no reflection coefficient or
wall model of a material system is asserted.

**(c) Robin interval model.** Fix $0<L<\infty$, real $\alpha,\beta$, read as
**declared boundary parameters** in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, a real $V\in
C([0,L];\mathbb R)$ and $\tilde V:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$ as in (b). The **Robin
interval model** declares the state space $L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$ and the
assigned energy operator
$$H_{\alpha\beta,V}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{\alpha\beta,V}):=\{u\in H^{2}(0,L):u'^{*}(0)=\alpha u^{*}(0),\ u'^{*}(L)=\beta u^{*}(L)\},$$
the operator $(\hbar^{2}/2m)\,A$ of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-separated-robin-green-resolvent]] with potential
$\tilde V$; the boundary parameters are declared model parameters, not derived
quantities, and no physical interpretation of a particular value of $\alpha$
or $\beta$ is asserted. The Dirichlet model of (b) is not the limit
$\alpha,\beta\to\infty$ in this definition; the Dirichlet condition is a
separate declared boundary condition.

**(d) Zero-range (delta) interface model.** Fix a real **coupling** $g$, read
in joule metres, and put $\alpha_{g}:=2mg/\hbar^{2}$, a real number in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. Let $A_{\alpha_{g}}$ be the delta interface operator of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-interface-operator]] on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$,
$$D(A_{\alpha_{g}})=\{u\in H^{1}(\mathbb R):u|_{(0,\infty)},u|_{(-\infty,0)}\in H^{2},\ u'^{*}(0+)-u'^{*}(0-)=\alpha_{g}u^{*}(0)\},\qquad A_{\alpha_{g}}u=-D^{2}u,$$
where the displayed action is understood piecewise: $(A_{\alpha_g}u)|_{(0,\infty)}=-D^2(u|_{(0,\infty)})$ and $(A_{\alpha_g}u)|_{(-\infty,0)}=-D^2(u|_{(-\infty,0)})$, with each weak derivative taken on that open half-line. The resulting two $L^2$ classes are glued across the null point $0$; $D^2u$ here is not the global weak second derivative on $\mathbb R$, which need not be an $L^2$ class when the first derivative jumps. Declare the **zero-range model** with coupling $g$ to be the model whose
assigned energy operator is
$$H_{g}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,A_{\alpha_{g}},\qquad D(H_{g}):=D(A_{\alpha_{g}}).$$
The interface condition $u'^{*}(0+)-u'^{*}(0-)=(2mg/\hbar^{2})u^{*}(0)$ is the
declared realization of a zero-range interaction at the origin: the pair reads
it as the model counterpart of a formally written term $g\,\delta(x)$ in the
energy expression, while recording that $\delta$ is not a function and that
the model is defined by the interface condition and not by an $L^{2}$
potential. The scaling of the operator is $(\hbar^{2}/2m)$ times the
mathematical operator, by the conventions of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]]. No identification of a
concrete impurity or material with the model is asserted.

**(e) Units, scope and status.** All three assignments are declared energy
operators with the joule as declared unit; the self-adjointness, spectra and
eigenbases of $H_{D,V}$, $H_{\alpha\beta,V}$ and $H_{g}$ are established by
the interval-spectra theorem and the zero-range bound-state theorem of this
page, and are not presupposed here. The boundary conditions, boundary parameters and coupling
are declared assumptions of the pair; nothing in this definition asserts that
a laboratory system realizes them, and no count, rate or measured value is
recorded.

The boundary conditions, boundary parameters and coupling are additional model assumptions of the pair; they are not derived from the line model, from P5 or from any material system, and no experiment, count or measured value is asserted. items.title: The line model's energy observable, flow and stationary states
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), all
read through the declared effective one-dimensional line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$
and spin label $s=0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $V:\mathbb
R\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, let $\|V\|_\infty=\sup|V|$,
and let $H_{V}$ be the assigned energy operator of clause (c) of the model,
with flow $U(t):=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ and evolved preparations
$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]. Then:

(a) $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model in the
sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]: $H_{V}$ is
densely defined and self-adjoint on
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$, bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$, and
$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}f+Vf$ for every $f\in D(H_{V})$.

(b) *Flow.* The family $t\mapsto U(t)$ is the model's strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group of the assigned energy observable; the
Schroedinger equation $i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{V}\psi(t)$ holds in the
norm-differentiable sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{V})$,
and for other vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not
asserted; density preparations evolve as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with
$\rho(t)$ a density operator for every $t$.

(c) *Stationary states.* For $\psi\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}$, $\psi\ne0$, the pure
preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for all $t$, if and
only if $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{V}$; in that case, with eigenvalue
$E$, one has $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$, the energy outcome law is
time-independent, and if $\|\psi\|=1$ the law assigns probability one to the
singleton $\{E\}$, so the energy mean exists and equals $E$, with second
moment $E^{2}$. Moreover every bounded assigned sharp observable compatible
with the energy has a time-independent outcome law in every preparation.

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit pure preparation $\psi$ the declared
position assignment of the model has outcome law
$\mu^{Q}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$ for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$;
and if $\psi$ is a unit eigenvector with eigenvalue $E$, the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ coexist as readings of the same
preparation, of the action of the declared observables, without any joint
measurement claim.

(e) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared
line model; it asserts no discrete spectrum or eigenbasis for a general
bounded measurable $V$, no completeness or scattering statement, no
identification of $H_{V}$ with any laboratory Hamiltonian beyond the tested

items.title: Rectangular barrier: scattering solution, flux balance and transmission
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]], with $m>0$, $\hbar>0$ and
energy, potential and position read in the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $a>0$, $U>E>0$ and let
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}U,&0<x<a,\\ 0&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$
let $k:=\sqrt{2mE}/\hbar$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{2m(U-E)}/\hbar$, and consider the
declared generalized stationary solutions of the model at energy $E$ (clause
(e) of the model) that are bounded, classically $C^{1}$ on $\mathbb R$ and
$C^{2}$ on each of $(-\infty,0),(0,a),(a,\infty)$. Then:

(a) *Scattering solution.* There is exactly one such $\psi$ with the
*transmission asymptotics*: $\psi(x)=e^{ikx}+re^{-ikx}$ for $x<0$ and
$\psi(x)=te^{ikx}$ for $x>a$, with uniquely determined $r,t\in\mathbb C$; with
$D:=2\cosh(\kappa a)+i\bigl(\frac{\kappa}{k}-\frac{k}{\kappa}\bigr)\sinh(\kappa a)$
one has $t=2e^{-ika}/D$, and
$$T:=|t|^{2}=\Bigl[1+\frac{U^{2}\sinh^{2}(\kappa a)}{4E(U-E)}\Bigr]^{-1},\qquad R:=|r|^{2}=1-T .$$

(b) *Conserved current and flux balance.* The declared probability current
$j(x):=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{\psi(x)}\psi'(x)\bigr)$
of the scattering solution is constant on $\mathbb R$, equal to
$\frac{\hbar k}{m}(1-|r|^{2})=\frac{\hbar k}{m}|t|^{2}$. With the **reference
current** $j_{\mathrm{in}}:=\frac{\hbar k}{m}$ of the unit-amplitude incoming
term $x\mapsto e^{ikx}$, the transmitted right-going current equals
$T\,j_{\mathrm{in}}$, the reflected left-going current has magnitude
$R\,j_{\mathrm{in}}$, and
$$T+R=1 .$$
The pair reads $T$ and $R$ as the transmitted and reflected fractions of the
reference current of the declared scattering solution; this reading is part of
the model and is not a measurement.

(c) *Thick-barrier form and error.* With $q:=e^{-2\kappa a}$ and
$C:=U^{2}/\bigl(4E(U-E)\bigr)$ one has
$$T=\frac{(4/C)\,q}{1+\bigl(\tfrac4C-2\bigr)q+q^{2}};$$
consequently, whenever $\delta:=\bigl(\tfrac4C-2\bigr)q+q^{2}$ satisfies
$|\delta|\le\frac12$,
$$\Bigl|T-\frac{16E(U-E)}{U^{2}}\,q\Bigr|\le\frac{32E(U-E)}{U^{2}}\,q\,|\delta| .$$

(d) *Scope.* The scattering solution $\psi$ is a declared generalized
stationary solution, not an element of $L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$; it is not
a preparation of the model, and no Born probability is read from it. The
numbers $T,R$ are exact model quantities of the declared solution, read as
ratios of currents under the model's scattering reading; the statement
contains no wave-packet construction, no time-dependent limit, no detector
response and no measured count, and it asserts neither that a particle passes
through the barrier nor that it is reflected.

items.title: Finite square well: bound-state conditions, simplicity and count
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$
and spin label $s=0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $a>0$,
$U>0$ and let
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}-U,&|x|<a,\\ 0,&|x|>a,\end{cases}$$
with arbitrary real endpoint values $V(-a)$ and $V(a)$, so that $V$ is a total bounded measurable function. It is read in joules, with $U$ in joules and $a$ in metres; let $H_{\mathrm w}$ be
the assigned energy operator of the line model with this potential, so that by
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]]
$D(H_{\mathrm w})=H^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and
$H_{\mathrm w}\psi=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+V\psi$; finally put
$K:=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar$. Then:

(a) $(H_{\mathrm w},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable; $H_{\mathrm
w}$ is self-adjoint on $H^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and bounded below.

(b) *Bound-state conditions.* For $E<0$ with $-U<E<0$ write
$\varepsilon:=-E$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{2m\varepsilon}/\hbar>0$ and
$k:=\sqrt{2m(U-\varepsilon)}/\hbar>0$, so that $k^{2}+\kappa^{2}=K^{2}$. Then
$E$ is an eigenvalue of $H_{\mathrm w}$ if and only if
$$k\tan(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(even case)}\qquad\text{or}\qquad -k\cot(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(odd case)} .$$
Every such eigenvalue is simple; its eigenfunction is, up to a nonzero scalar,
$x\mapsto\cos(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by $ce^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside in the
even case, and $x\mapsto\sin(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by
$c\,\operatorname{sgn}(x)e^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside in the odd case. No $E\le-U$
and no $E\ge0$ is an eigenvalue, so every eigenvalue of $H_{\mathrm w}$ lies in
$(-U,0)$; the bound-state energies of the model are exactly these eigenvalues,
and each bound state is stationary with energy equal to its eigenvalue.

(c) *Count.* The number of negative eigenvalues of $H_{\mathrm w}$ equals
$\bigl\lceil 2aK/\pi\bigr\rceil$; more precisely, the equations of (b) have
exactly one solution $k$ in each interval
$\bigl(\frac{n\pi}{2a},\frac{(n+1)\pi}{2a}\bigr)$, $n\ge0$, whose left
endpoint satisfies $\frac{n\pi}{2a}<K$, and no solution in $(0,K)$ elsewhere,
and the solutions are alternatively of even type ($n$ even) and odd type
($n$ odd). In particular $H_{\mathrm w}$ has at least one bound state for all
$a,U>0$.

(d) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared well
data $a,U$ and the cited mathematics; the energies are read in joules when
$a$ is in metres, $U$ in joules and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. No material
well, impurity or measured spectrum is identified with the model, and no
empirical result is asserted.

items.title: Interval models: discrete spectra, complete eigenbases, min-max bounds and nodal counts
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), read
through the declared interval models
[[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]] with $0<L<\infty$,
$m>0$, $\hbar>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a real
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$ put $\tilde V:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, so that the assigned
energy operators of the definition satisfy
$H_{D,V}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)(A_{D}+M_{\tilde V})$ and
$H_{\alpha\beta,V}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{\alpha\beta,\tilde V}$. Then:

(a) *Dirichlet interval model.* $(H_{D,V},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp
observable; $H_{D,V}$ is self-adjoint with compact resolvent and has a complete
orthonormal family $(\psi_{n})_{n\ge1}$ of eigenvectors. Its eigenvalues,
listed with multiplicity, form a sequence
$\mathcal E_{1}\le\mathcal E_{2}\le\cdots$ with
$\mathcal E_{n}\to\infty$ and
$\sigma(H_{D,V})=\{\mathcal E_{n}:n\ge1\}$, and no other spectral points; each
eigenspace is one-dimensional, so the list is strict,
$\mathcal E_{1}<\mathcal E_{2}<\cdots$, and the eigenvector belonging to
$\mathcal E_{n}$ has exactly $n-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$. The min-max comparison
$$\Bigl|\mathcal E_{n}-\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}}{2mL^{2}}\Bigr| \le\|V\|_{\infty}\qquad(n\ge1)$$
holds. If $V=0$, the eigenpairs of $H_{D,0}$ are exactly the pairs
$\bigl(\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}}{2mL^{2}},\,e_{n}\bigr)$ with
$e_{n}(x)=\sqrt{2/L}\,\sin(n\pi x/L)$, $n\ge1$, a complete orthonormal family of
$L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$.

(b) *Robin interval model.* For real $\alpha,\beta$ (the declared boundary
parameters in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$), $(H_{\alpha\beta,V},\mathrm J)$ is an
assigned sharp observable; $H_{\alpha\beta,V}$ is self-adjoint with compact
resolvent; it has a complete orthonormal eigenfamily, every eigenspace is
one-dimensional, its spectrum consists exactly of its eigenvalues, which can
be listed strictly increasingly as $\mathcal E_{1}<\mathcal E_{2}<\cdots$ with
$\mathcal E_{n}\to\infty$, and its essential spectrum is empty. With
$\lambda_{n}:=2m\mathcal E_{n}/\hbar^{2}$ and $u_{a}(\cdot,\lambda)$ the unique
$C^{2}$ solution of $-u''+\tilde Vu=\lambda u$ with $u(0)=1$, $u'(0)=\alpha$,
one has $u_{a}(L,\lambda_{n})\ne0$ and
$$\beta=\frac{u_{a}'(L,\lambda_{n})}{u_{a}(L,\lambda_{n})}\qquad(n\ge1).$$

(c) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, on the declared
boundary conditions and on the cited mathematics. The boundary conditions and
parameters are declared model assumptions; the eigenvalues are read in joules
when $V$ and $\hbar$ enter in the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. No laboratory wall, box or
surface is identified with the boundary conditions, no measured spectrum is
asserted, and no completeness of any continuum or scattering object is
claimed.

items.title: The zero-range (delta) model: self-adjointness and its unique bound state
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] and the declared zero-range
model of [[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]] clause (d) with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, coupling $g\in\mathbb R$ (in joule
metres) and $\alpha_{g}=2mg/\hbar^{2}$. Let
$H_{g}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{\alpha_{g}}$ be the assigned energy operator of the
zero-range model on the domain $D(H_{g})=D(A_{\alpha_{g}})$ of the interface
operator. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_{g})$ consists exactly of the classes $u\in H^{1}(\mathbb R)$ whose
restrictions to $(0,\infty)$ and $(-\infty,0)$ are of class $H^{2}$, subject to
the interface condition
$$u'^{*}(0+)-u'^{*}(0-)=\frac{2mg}{\hbar^{2}}\,u^{*}(0),$$
On that domain, $(H_gu)|_{\mathbb R_\pm}=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2(u|_{\mathbb R_\pm})$, where $\mathbb R_+=(0,\infty)$, $\mathbb R_-=(-\infty,0)$ and each second weak derivative is taken on its open half-line; these two $L^2$ classes are glued across the null point $0$. The action is not the global weak second derivative of $u$ on $\mathbb R$. $(H_{g},\mathrm J)$ is
an assigned sharp observable: $H_{g}$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on
$D(H_{g})$.

(b) *Repulsive and free couplings.* If $g\ge0$, then $H_{g}$ has no negative
eigenvalue, and for every $g\in\mathbb R$ the value $0$ is not an eigenvalue of
$H_{g}$.

(c) *Attractive coupling.* If $g<0$, then $H_{g}$ has exactly one negative
eigenvalue, namely
$$E_{g}=-\frac{mg^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}<0,$$
and its eigenspace is one-dimensional, spanned by the unit class
$$\psi_{g}(x)=\sqrt{\frac{m|g|}{\hbar^{2}}}\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{m|g|}{\hbar^{2}}|x|\Bigr).$$
This eigenpair is the unique bound state of the zero-range model: every
eigenvector of $H_{g}$ with negative eigenvalue is a nonzero multiple of
$\psi_{g}$, the preparation $[\psi_{g}]$ is stationary with energy $E_{g}$, and
the energy outcome law assigns probability one to $\{E_{g}\}$.

(d) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
interface realization and the cited mathematics; the coupling $g$ is a
declared model parameter, not a measured quantity. No scattering coefficient,
no transmission or reflection statement, no material impurity and no measured
spectrum is asserted; the formal writing $g\,\delta(x)$ is not used as a
function and no potential in $L^{2}$ is involved.

items.title: What the one-dimensional potentials page establishes, assumes and defers
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**What is established.** The page fixes a declared effective one-dimensional
model of a spinless massive particle
([[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]]) and proves, as
conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5 and the cited mathematics, the
following statements. The mathematical lemmas
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]] and
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] identify the
free operator with the weak second-derivative operator and transfer
self-adjointness, resolvents, spectra and eigenfamilies along positive
scaling; [[lem-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-flux-identity]] proves the
one-dimensional continuity identity and the constancy of the current of a
stationary solution.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-line-model-energy-and-stationary-states]] establishes
that the declared energy operator of the line model with a real bounded
measurable potential is an assigned sharp observable, generates the unitary
flow of the model, and that its stationary preparations are exactly the
eigenrays with point-mass energy law.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-interval-spectra-completeness-and-nodes]] establishes,
for the declared Dirichlet and separated Robin interval models with continuous
real potentials, self-adjointness with compact resolvent, complete
orthonormal eigenbases, discreteness and simplicity of the spectra, the
min-max comparison of the Dirichlet energies with the free box energies and
the nodal counts, together with the Robin eigenvalue condition.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-finite-well-bound-states]] gives the exact root
conditions, simplicity, parity and count of the bound states of the finite
square well, and
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-delta-point-interaction-bound-state]] gives the
self-adjointness of the declared zero-range interface operator and its unique
bound state for attractive coupling with the exact energy
$-mg^{2}/(2\hbar^{2})$. [[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]]
gives the unique scattering solution of the rectangular barrier, its conserved
current, the exact coefficients $T$ and $R$, the flux balance $T+R=1$, the
reading of $T$ and $R$ as fractions of the reference current, and the
thick-barrier error bound.

**What is assumed, not derived.** The page's model data are declared, not
derived: the reduction of the three-dimensional massive-particle model to one
spatial dimension, the position and momentum assignments of the line model,
the Dirichlet and Robin boundary conditions with their boundary parameters,
the zero-range interface condition with its coupling, and the scattering
reading of the current ratios. Each is an assumption of the pair in the sense
of the preparation and apparatus discipline P7; an identification of a
concrete material system with any of them is a tested identification with
uncertainty and is not produced by these items. The operators rest on the
mathematical supplier [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
and on the interval and contact mathematics of
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] and the items of the intervals
pair, whose Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice hypotheses are inherited by
every consumer above.

**What is not addressed.** No wave-packet or time-dependent scattering limit
is computed; no arrival-time, detector-response, efficiency or background
model is declared; no count, rate, cross-section or measured spectrum appears.
The scattering solution of the barrier item is not an element of the model
state space, so no Born probability is read from it. Potentials with
unbounded or singular growth, the harmonic oscillator, the Coulomb problem,
higher-dimensional scattering, resonant and above-barrier behaviour, and the
Airy/WKB connection problem for smooth barriers belong to other pages of the
category and are not consumed or anticipated here. The example page of the
pair carries exact finite checks of the barrier and well formulas; those are
model computations, not measurements.

**Evidence status.** The page is a conditional model development. It contains
no experiment, no reported observation, no uncertainty statement and no
statistical inference; agreement of any of its formulas with data would be
evidence about the combined model, apparatus and analysis assumptions and
would not prove the model.

items.title: Tunnelling through a rectangular barrier: an exactly solvable scaling and its thick-barrier comparison
items.statement:
Work in the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$,
action constant $\hbar>0$, and lengths, energies and currents read in the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Declare the incident
energy $E>0$ and the barrier height $U:=2E$, so that
$\kappa:=\sqrt{2m(U-E)}/\hbar=\sqrt{2mE}/\hbar=:k$; declare further the barrier
width $a:=\ln(10)/\kappa>0$, so that $\kappa a=\ln 10$ and
$e^{\kappa a}=10$. Consider the scattering solution of
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]] for this barrier and
set $q:=e^{-2\kappa a}$. Then, as exact identities in the model:

(i) $C:=U^{2}/(4E(U-E))=1$, $q=1/100$, and
$$T=\frac{400}{10201},\qquad R=1-T=\frac{9801}{10201};$$

(ii) with rational brackets,
$$\frac{3921}{100000}<T<\frac{3922}{100000},\qquad \frac{96078}{100000}<R<\frac{96079}{100000};$$

(iii) the thick-barrier approximation value is
$\frac{16E(U-E)}{U^{2}}q=\frac{1}{25}$, the exact difference is
$$T-\frac{1}{25}=-\frac{201}{255025},$$
which lies between $-0.000789$ and $-0.000788$, and the error bound of the
theorem reads
$$\Bigl|T-\frac1{25}\Bigr|\le\frac{201}{125000}=0.001608 ;$$

(iv) since $q=1/100>0$, the transmission $T$ is positive although the
barrier is classically forbidden at this energy; and by clause (b) of the
barrier theorem the number $T$ is the transmitted fraction of the reference
current $j_{\mathrm{in}}=\hbar k/m$ of the declared scattering solution, while
$R$ is the reflected fraction.

The example is an exact computation in the declared barrier model with
declared data $U,E,a,m,\hbar$ related as above; it records no measurement and
no apparatus value.

items.title: Finite square well: an exactly solvable bound state and exact bound-state counts
items.statement:
Work in the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$
and action constant $\hbar>0$, energies, lengths and the depth $U$ read in the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and consider the finite
square well $V(x)=-U$ for $|x|\le a$, $V(x)=0$ for $|x|>a$ of
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-finite-well-bound-states]] with half-width $a>0$ and
depth $U>0$.

(i) *Exact boundary case of the first branch.* Declare
$$U:=\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}}{16ma^{2}} .$$
Then $K=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar=\pi\sqrt2/(4a)$, the count parameter is
$2aK/\pi=\sqrt2/2$, there is exactly one bound state, it is an even
(cosine-type) state, and its binding energy is exactly
$$E=-\frac{U}{2}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}}{32ma^{2}} .$$
For this declared depth the root of the even condition is exactly
$k=\kappa=\pi/(4a)$.

(ii) *Exact counts at declared depths.* With
$$U:=\frac{25\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}}{32ma^{2}}$$
one has $K=5\pi/(4a)$ and $2aK/\pi=5/2$, so there are exactly three bound
states, with types even, odd and even in order of increasing energy. With
$U:=\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}/(8ma^{2})$ one has $K=\pi/(2a)$ and exactly one bound
state; with $U:=\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}/(2ma^{2})$ one has $K=\pi/a$ and exactly two
bound states. For every declared depth $U>0$ there is at least one bound
state.

(iii) *Rational bracket of the first case.*
$$\frac{707}{1000}<\frac{2aK}{\pi}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}<\frac{708}{1000},$$
so the count $\lceil 2aK/\pi\rceil$ equals one in case (i).

The example is a conditional computation in the declared well model and
asserts no measured binding energy; the identities in (i) and (ii) are exact in
the model at the displayed declared data.

items.title: The Dirichlet box: exact spectrum, nodes, constant shift and gaps
items.statement:
Work in the declared Dirichlet interval model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]] clause (b) with
$0<L<\infty$, mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$, and energies in joules
under [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then, as exact identities
in the model:

(i) *Free box.* For $V=0$ the eigenpairs of the assigned energy operator
$H_{D,0}$ are exactly
$$\Bigl(\mathcal E_{n},\,e_{n}\Bigr),\qquad \mathcal E_{n}=\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}}{2mL^{2}},\qquad e_{n}(x)=\sqrt{\frac2L}\,\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\quad n\ge1,$$
the family $(e_{n})_{n\ge1}$ is a complete orthonormal family of
$L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$, each eigenvalue is simple, and $e_{n}$ has exactly
$n-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$, namely the points $x_{k}=kL/n$, $k=1,\dots,n-1$.

(ii) *Constant shift.* If $V=c$ is the constant potential of value $c\in
\mathbb R$ (joules), then $H_{D,c}$ has exactly the same eigenfunctions
$e_{n}$ and the eigenvalues $\mathcal E_{n}+c$; consequently the min-max
complexity bound of the interval theorem is attained with equality,
$|\mathcal E_{n}+c-\mathcal E_{n}|=|c|=\|V\|_{\infty}$ for every $n$.

(iii) *Gaps.* $\mathcal E_{n+1}-\mathcal E_{n}
=\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}(2n+1)}{2mL^{2}}>0$, so the spectrum is strictly
increasing.

The example is an exact conditional computation in the declared box model
and asserts no measured transition energy.

items.title: What the one-dimensional potentials examples establish
items.statement:
## Scope of the examples page

**The three computations.**
[[ex-nrqm-potentials-rectangular-barrier-tunnelling-and-thick-limit]] treats
the rectangular barrier of [[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]]
at the exactly solvable scaling $U=2E$ with $\kappa a=\ln 10$: it obtains
$T=400/10201$ and $R=9801/10201$ as exact rationals, brackets them by
$3921/100000<T<3922/100000$, compares the exact value with the thick-barrier
value $1/25$ (the difference is exactly $-201/255025$) and verifies the
theorem's error bound $201/125000=0.001608$; the computation is a finite check
of the model formulas, including the positivity of transmission through a
classically forbidden barrier.
[[ex-nrqm-potentials-finite-well-exact-root-and-count]] exhibits a declared
well depth at which the unique bound state is exactly solvable (even state,
$k=\kappa=\pi/(4a)$, binding energy $E=-U/2=-\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}/(32ma^{2})$),
verifies the even root condition with the special value $\tan(\pi/4)=1$, and
verifies the count and branch criterion at declared depths: exactly three
bound states with types even, odd, even when $2aK/\pi=5/2$, exactly one when
$2aK/\pi=1$, exactly two when $2aK/\pi=2$, and at least one for every
$a,U>0$.
[[ex-nrqm-potentials-box-spectrum-and-nodes]] records the exact free Dirichlet
box eigenpairs $\mathcal E_{n}=\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}/(2mL^{2})$ with sine
eigenfunctions, their explicit $n-1$ nodal points $kL/n$, the exact spectrum
$\mathcal E_{n}+c$ of a constant potential with the min-max bound attained,
and the positive gaps $\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}(2n+1)/(2mL^{2})$.

**What is and is not compared.** The comparisons are internal: the exact
barrier formula and its thick-barrier approximation, the exact well root
condition and the exact branch count, and the exact box spectrum with the
min-max bound. They verify the cited theorems at declared parameter points by
exact rational and algebraic checks; they are not numerical approximations of
generic transcendental roots, they contain no simulation presented as data,
and they report no measured value, no uncertainty and no significance
statement. The only numerical decimals displayed are brackets of exact
rationals proven in the verifications.

**Evidence status.** All three items are conditional computations in the
declared line, well and box models of the pair's A page, under the same P1,
P2, P4, P5 assumptions and the same cited mathematics; the empirical
qualifications of the A page carry over unchanged. Nothing on this page is an
observation, an apparatus model or a statistical inference, and agreement of
the displayed identities with any measurement would be evidence about the
combined model and apparatus assumptions rather than a proof of the model.
